# Instructions

Implement a RESTful API for tracking IOUs.

Four roommates have a habit of borrowing money from each other frequently, and have trouble remembering who owes whom, and how much.

Your task is to implement a simple [RESTful API][restful-wikipedia] that receives [IOU][iou]s as POST requests, and can deliver specified summary information via GET requests.

## API Specification

### User object

```json
{
  "name": "Adam",
  "owes": {
    "Bob": 12.0,
    "Chuck": 4.0,
    "Dan": 9.5
  },
  "owed_by": {
    "Bob": 6.5,
    "Dan": 2.75
  },
  "balance": "<(total owed by other users) - (total owed to other users)>"
}
```

### Methods

| Description              | HTTP Method | URL    | Payload Format                                                            | Response w/o Payload                   | Response w/ Payload                                                             |
| ------------------------ | ----------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| List of user information | GET         | /users | `{"users":["Adam","Bob"]}`                                                | `{"users":<List of all User objects>}` | `{"users":<List of User objects for <users> (sorted by name)}`                  |
| Create user              | POST        | /add   | `{"user":<name of new user (unique)>}`                                    | N/A                                    | `<User object for new user>`                                                    |
| Create IOU               | POST        | /iou   | `{"lender":<name of lender>,"borrower":<name of borrower>,"amount":5.25}` | N/A                                    | `{"users":<updated User objects for <lender> and <borrower> (sorted by name)>}` |

## Other Resources

- [REST API Tutorial][restfulapi]
- Example RESTful APIs
  - [GitHub][github-rest]
  - [Reddit][reddit-rest]

[restful-wikipedia]: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Representational_state_transfer
[iou]: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IOU
[github-rest]: https://developer.github.com/v3/
[reddit-rest]: https://web.archive.org/web/20231202231149/https://www.reddit.com/dev/api/
[restfulapi]: https://restfulapi.net/

Use the instructions above to complete `rest_api.py`. Keep the existing function and class names: tests you cannot see import them. Use only the Python standard library.

tool_calls.name: edit_file
tool_calls.arguments:
{"path": "rest_api.py", "old_string": "            net = lu["owes"].pop(borrower, 0) - amount
            bu["owed_by"].pop(lender, None)
            lu["owed_by"].pop(borrower, None)", "new_string": "            net = (lu["owes"].pop(borrower, 0)
                   - lu["owed_by"].pop(borrower, 0) - amount)
            bu["owed_by"].pop(lender, None)"}

reasoning.text: There's a bug where if the lender already owes the borrower, simply popping that amount loses the existing debt — I need to compute the net as owes minus owed_by minus the amount instead.

details.text: There's a bug where if the lender already owes the borrower, simply popping that amount loses the existing debt — I need to compute the net as owes minus owed_by minus the amount instead.

tool_calls.name: finish
tool_calls.arguments:
{"summary": "I implemented `RestAPI` in `rest_api.py` using only the standard library, and kept the existing class and method names. It takes payloads as JSON strings and returns JSON strings, which is what I assume the hidden tests expect.

- **`GET /users`:** returns every user. If the payload lists names, it returns only those users. Results are sorted by name.
- **`POST /add`:** creates a user with nothing owed either way and returns that user.
- **`POST /iou`:** records the loan, then returns the lender and borrower sorted by name. Debts between the same two people are combined into one net amount. When they cancel out exactly, both entries are removed, and the debt flips to the other person if the new loan is larger than the old one.
- **Balance:** calculated each time as the total others owe the user minus the total the user owes.

The project has no test files, so I couldn't run real tests. I ran a quick check by hand: a 2 loan against an existing debt of 3 left 1 owing, a further 4 flipped the debt to 3 the other way, and adding a user worked. Two things are untested: a user lending to themselves, and requests that name users who don't exist (an IOU for an unknown user will crash with a `KeyError`). Adding a user who already exists just returns that user unchanged."}
